endorsements.quote: The SDiPath guidelines affirm that DIA/AI intended for diagnostic use needs to be designed in compliance with current laws and regulatory requirements for medical devices, i.e., only officially certified systems (e.g., IVD-CE certified, FDA-approved) or lab-developed systems properly validated with respect to quality control and quality assurance can be applied.
Also, and equally important, it is the board-certified pathologist who determines and is legally responsible for the finally rendered diagnosis.

An internal validation of the system on relevant specimens mirroring the real-world clinical use is recommended, even if the system is officially certified (e.g., IVD-CE certified, FDA-approved) to ensure consistency of performance.
When validating the system, a concordance testing needs to be carried out and revalidation shall be performed whenever changes are made in the workflow.
User training, personnel, and technical requirements, as well as SOPs for hardware and software malfunctions and management updates, need to be provided.

In short, the DIA/AI systems need to be well integrated into the pathology workflow environment and automated, in order to enable streamlining of the diagnostic process in the era of increasing workload.

unlisted_practices: Store the results of DIA/AI analysis to allow diagnosis retracing.
Document all steps of DIA/AI use in a standard operating procedure (SOP) document.
Document scan metadata, the software used, the validation protocol, and software performance (reproducibility, intra-observer variability, known problems).
Perform quality control steps verifying that scans are suitable for analysis and that all relevant areas have been analyzed.
Include information about the DIA/AI system used, including quality control measures and validation steps, in the pathology report.
Provide pathologists visual control of algorithm results, highlighting the regions that determined the output.
Enable a feedback loop in DIA/AI systems to improve performance.
Review and update the recommendations as technology advances.

screen.reason: Consensus Delphi recommendations and best practices from the Swiss Digital Pathology Consortium on implementing digital image analysis and AI in routine pathology diagnostics.
